questions.solution:
From both dices, J is common and on the same surface. So, all remaining surface will be opposite to each other.

So, T will be opposite to X.

questions.question: Which number will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 14 − 45 × 5 + 6 ÷ 3 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
Which number will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?
14 − 45 × 5 + 6 ÷ 3 = ?
questions.solution:
Given equation: 14 − 45 × 5 + 6 ÷ 3 = ?

Now, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged, then:

⇒ 14 + 45  ÷ 5 − 6  × 3 = ? ⇒ 14 + 9 − 18 = ? ⇒ 23 − 18 = 5.

questions.question: In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All necklaces are squares. Some squares are circles. No circle is a ring. Conclusions: I.No square is a ring. II.No ring is a circle. III.Some squares are necklaces.
questions.questionHtml:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements
to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically
follow(s) from the statements.
Statements:
All necklaces are squares.
Some squares are circles.
No circle is a ring.
Conclusions:
I.No square is a ring.
II.No ring is a circle.
III.Some squares are necklaces.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow.
options.html: Only conclusions II and III follow.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow.
options.html: Only conclusions I and III follow.

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. No square is a ring. - False (because there is no direct relation given between them so it can be possible but not definite)

II. No ring is a circle. - True (because No circle is a ring given, so No ring is a circle it is definite)

III. Some squares are necklaces. - True (because All necklaces are squares given, so Some squares are also necklaces)

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A x B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, if M + Q – R + K – Y, then how is M related to Y?
questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’;
‘A – B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’;
‘A x B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and
‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’.
Based on the above, if M + Q – R + K – Y, then how is M related to Y?
questions.solution:
M is the mother of Q, Q is the brother of R, R is the mother of K and K is the brother of Y.

​

So, M is the Mother’s mother of Y.

questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 29 × 145 + 5 − 640 ÷ 15 = 216
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?
29 × 145 + 5 − 640 ÷ 15 = 216
questions.solution:
Option 1) ÷ and +

Two signs need to be interchanged then:

⇒ 29 × 145 ÷ 5 − 640 + 15 = 216

⇒ 29 × 29 − 640 + 15 = 216

⇒ 841 − 640 + 15 = 216

⇒ 856 − 640 = 216

⇒ 216 = 216
